title: Texas's 36th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 36th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Brian Babin against Democratic challenger Rhonda Hart. Babin has represented the district since 2015 and currently serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology. The district underwent mid-decade redistricting in 2025, losing Liberty County and extending north to Lufkin, while maintaining its strongly Republican tilt (Cook PVI: R+12). Hart, an Army veteran and gun-safety activist whose daughter was killed in the 2018 Santa Fe High School shooting, is making her second bid for Congress after an unsuccessful run in TX-14 in 2024. The general election will be held on November 3, 2026, following primary elections on March 3, 2026.
polling_note: No district-specific public opinion polls were found for Texas's 36th Congressional District race. Statewide generic ballot polls for Texas from June 2026 showed Republicans leading Democrats 49% to 43% (Texas A&M University/ReconMR), but these are not specific to this district.

candidates.name: Brian Babin
candidates.summary: Brian Babin is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 36th Congressional District, first elected in 2014. He serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and previously chaired the Space Subcommittee. A dentist by profession and U.S. Air Force veteran, Babin focuses on border security, tax cuts, Second Amendment rights, and space exploration. He has held the seat since 2015 and won the 2026 Republican primary with 81.1% of the vote against challenger Jonathan Mitchell.

candidates.name: Rhonda Hart
candidates.summary: Rhonda Hart is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 36th Congressional District. An Army veteran who served from 2000 to 2003, her daughter Kimberly Vaughan was killed in the 2018 Santa Fe High School shooting, leading Hart to become a prominent gun-safety activist. She previously ran for Congress in Texas's 14th Congressional District in 2024. Hart advocates for common-sense gun laws, women's reproductive rights, and improved veterans' healthcare. She won the 2026 Democratic primary with 64.1% of the vote, defeating Doug Rogers.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling exists for this race, which limits confidence to medium. However, the structural data strongly favors the incumbent. Brian Babin is a six-term incumbent (first elected 2014) and current Chairman of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee. He won his 2026 primary with 81.1% of the vote. The district's Cook PVI is R+12 and the 2025 redistricting maintained its strongly Republican tilt. The only broader polling signal—a June 2026 Texas generic ballot showing Republicans ahead 49% to 43%—is consistent with a Republican advantage. Rhonda Hart is a credible Democratic nominee (Army veteran and gun-safety activist) and won her primary with 64.1%, but the district's partisan lean combined with Babin's incumbency and fundraising/chairship advantages make the Republican nominee a clear favorite. A likely_r rating (92% win probability, ~17-point margin estimate) reflects that the seat is not quite safe—a Democratic longshot win is possible if national dynamics shift dramatically—but Babin holds a commanding structural edge.
